title: Sheet-fed chart reader
summary: A device that pulls a chart page in by itself, finds the rows and reads them, like the X-Rite i1iSis.
experience_text: No recording of a sheet-fed reader has reached us yet. This list is our best reasoning from the table and handheld work: the same start states, readings and endings, adapted to a device that feeds the paper itself. If your program offers something this list misses, please tell us.
before_you_start: The reader, its cables, and the program you normally use, closed for now.
Two printed chart pages the reader can read (a chart of two pages is ideal), and one plain sheet of the same paper.
Some readers must be switched on before their USB cable is plugged in: do it the way the maker says.
The maker's manual wins: if a block contradicts it, follow the manual and skip the block.
Unplug other USB devices you can do without (disks, memory sticks, phones, printers). A keyboard and a mouse may stay.

blocks.label: switch-on
blocks.title: Switch on and start the program
steps: Make sure the program is closed and the reader is off.
Start this block (the recording starts now).
Switch the reader on (and plug in its USB cable, if that is the maker's order), and wait until it is quiet.
Start the program and wait until it says the reader is ready.
blocks.note: Did the reader do anything by itself at the start (move rollers, light up, calibrate)?
blocks.why: The start of a just-switched-on reader is the first thing ChromIQ must repeat exactly.

blocks.label: calibrate
blocks.title: Calibrate
blocks.only_if: If the program has no separate calibration, record 30 seconds of the program waiting instead and say so in the note.
steps: Start this block.
Start the calibration in the program, if it has one.
Wait until the program says it is done.
blocks.note: Was there a separate calibration, or does the reader calibrate by itself?
blocks.why: Where a reader calibrates (an inner tile, a white strip on the page) changes every reading after it.

blocks.label: page-to-end
blocks.title: One chart page to the end, saved
steps: Start this block.
Feed the first chart page, as the program asks, and let it read the whole page.
Let the reader push the page out.
Save the measurement in the program under a name you will recognise, and send that file together with the zip.
blocks.note: How did the page go in (by itself, after a button)? The name of the saved file.
blocks.why: One whole page, from feeding to the saved result, is the core job ChromIQ would drive, and pairing it with the program's own file lets us check every number.

blocks.label: second-page
blocks.title: The next page of the chart
blocks.only_if: Only if your chart has more than one page.
steps: Start this block.
Feed the second page when the program asks for it, and let it be read to the end.
blocks.note: Did the program check that it was the right page (a barcode, a mark)?
blocks.why: How the program tells pages apart decides how ChromIQ prints and reads multi-page charts.

blocks.label: wrong-sheet
blocks.title: A plain sheet instead of a chart
steps: Start this block.
Start a reading, and feed the plain sheet instead of a chart page.
Read what the program says, and answer it the normal way.
blocks.note: What exactly did the program say, and what did the reader do with the sheet?
blocks.why: A refused sheet is an ending ChromIQ must recognise and explain; only a recording shows how the reader reports it.

blocks.label: cancel-reading
blocks.title: Cancel while a page is being read
steps: Start this block.
Feed a chart page and start the reading.
While the page is moving through the reader, press Cancel or Stop in the program.
Wait until the reader is at rest, and take the page out the way the program says.
blocks.note: What happened to the page? Did the program ask you to do anything?
blocks.why: A cancel with paper inside is the ending most likely to leave a device in a strange state.

blocks.label: modes
blocks.title: Every other reading mode
blocks.only_if: Only the modes your program offers.
steps: Start this block.
For each other mode or measurement condition the program offers (for example M1, M2, UV, a faster or slower setting), read one page.
Before each page, type the setting's name here and press Enter.
blocks.note: The settings you tried, in order.
blocks.why: Each mode may be its own set of commands, and ChromIQ can only offer what it has seen.

blocks.label: eject
blocks.title: The program's eject or feed controls
blocks.only_if: Only if the program has such buttons.
steps: Start this block.
Use each paper control the program offers (eject, feed, clean) once, with no paper inside.
Before each one, type its name here and press Enter.
blocks.note: Which controls, and what each did.
blocks.why: Each control is a command ChromIQ could offer for the same purpose, for example to free a page.

blocks.label: idle
blocks.title: Five quiet minutes
steps: Start this block.
With the program open and no paper inside, do nothing for five minutes.
blocks.note: Did anything happen on its own?
blocks.why: Programs often keep talking to an idle device; ChromIQ must know what keeps it ready.

blocks.label: cable-pull
blocks.title: Pull the cable and plug it back
steps: Start this block (the recording keeps going while the reader is gone).
With no paper inside and the program idle, pull the reader's USB cable.
Wait 10 seconds, plug it back in, and wait until the program shows the reader again.
blocks.why: A pulled cable is an ending ChromIQ must survive without needing the maker's program.

blocks.label: close
blocks.title: Close the program
steps: Start this block.
Close the program the normal way, and wait 10 seconds.
blocks.note: Did the reader do anything when the program closed?
blocks.why: What the program sends when it closes is what ChromIQ should do when it lets go of the reader.

blocks.label: unexpected-end
blocks.title: The program ends by force while a chart page is being read, then starts again
steps: Start this block.
Start a chart page is being read in the program.
While it is busy, end the program by force (Windows: Task Manager (Ctrl+Shift+Esc), select the program, End task. Mac: Apple menu > Force Quit, select the program, Force Quit.) Type killed.
Wait 20 seconds. Start the program again and note what it does with the instrument (a new calibration, a message).
Take the page out the way the maker's manual says.
blocks.note: What did the instrument do when the program disappeared, and when it came back?
blocks.why: After an unexpected end the instrument is left as the program left it; how the maker's program recovers is what ChromIQ needs after its own unexpected end.

blocks.label: questions
blocks.title: A few questions
steps: No recording now. Answer the questions below; a short line each is fine.
questions: Which program and which version did you use, on which system?
Which chart did you use, and what paper size? If you can, send the chart file too.
What does the printed chart have besides patches (marks, a barcode, a white strip)?
Does the program offer anything that these blocks did not cover?
blocks.why: What is printed around the patches is what ChromIQ must print on its own charts for the reader to accept them.
